sources_considered.why: Independent study comparing SWE-bench passes with real maintainer merge decisions. Directly tests Part A.
Rényi Institute report that GPT-5.2 solved open Erdős problems, citing Terence Tao's database. Bears on Part C.
GDPval-AA is itself a benchmark, which the speaker dismisses, so it cannot show real-world success.
Remote Labor Index results from October 2025 fall outside the target period, and I could not verify later figures from a primary source.
News coverage of Tao's caveats. The point is noted in limitations; I used the institutional source instead.

receipt.public_excerpt: the automated grader is on average about 24.2 percentage points (standard error: 2.7) higher than the maintainer merge decision. This is strong and statistically significant evidence that the naive interpretation of the benchmark as passing maintainer review is misleading.

evidence_items.explanation: Real maintainers would reject roughly half of the coding-benchmark passes. That supports Part A: benchmark gains overstate real-world success. METR adds that benchmarks still carry signal, and its newest model tested is Claude Sonnet 4.5.

evidence_items.publisher: HUN-REN Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics

receipt.public_excerpt: ChatGPT 5. 2 Thinking and 5.2 Pro provided complete, correct solutions to Erdős problems 205 and 652 (previous research in the literature has not revealed any relevant partial or complete solutions to these problems).

evidence_items.explanation: A recent model solved open math problems, recorded in Tao's database, within the 'last few months'. That is a documented real-world result outside coding, which cuts against Part C.

unresolved_gaps: METR's study covers models up to Claude Sonnet 4.5 (late 2025), not the newest early-2026 models.
Tao and others called the Erdős solutions 'low-hanging fruit', so how much they show broad extension beyond coding is open to debate.
I did not read Tao's GitHub database directly.
